- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect risk of rebound or mean reversion.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5+ in 3-5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1-2% for the next 3-5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a slight downward bias (−0.5 to −1.5%) for 5-7 days if recent price is above 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., first 5-7 days); apply a 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive positive values), model often fails to adjust for volatility; add a volatility buffer (e.g., ±1.5% band) around forecast to account for overconfidence.
